started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

You'll usually be responsible for a child if you live with them.

Alex is 11 years old (under 16) and lives with you in the UK. This means you meet the basic eligibility criteria.

## **Eligibility Decision: ELIGIBLE**

**Good news!** You are **eligible** to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

### Why you're eligible:

✓ You live in the UK  
✓ Alex is 11 years old (under 16)  
✓ Alex lives with you  
✓ You are responsible for Alex's care  
✓ None of the disqualifying circumstances apply (Alex is not in care, hospital, fostered with council payments, working 24+ hours, or receiving disqualifying benefits)

### What you should know:

- **Only one person can claim Child Benefit for the same child.** If another adult in your household (such as another parent) also wants to claim, you'll need to agree between yourselves who will claim. If you can't agree, HMRC will decide.

- **High Income Child Benefit tax charge:** If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay a tax charge. You can still claim Child Benefit but may need to pay some or all of it back through tax.

### Next steps:

You can proceed to [make a claim for Child Benefit](https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim) for Alex.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
